text:
maya: hey team — opened a small TF change that wires route propagation for the new GPU subnets. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/3421 can someone take a quick look? :eyes:
aj: can you paste the plan output or the snippet of the change? want to see if this touches any shared route tables
maya: sure — it only adds a route that points to the gpu NAT gateway and enables propagate on the peering attachment. snippet:
```hcl
resource "aws_route" "gpu_egress" {
  route_table_id         = var.gpu_route_table_id
  destination_cidr_block = "0.0.0.0/0"
  nat_gateway_id         = aws_nat_gateway.gpu.id
}

resource "aws_vpc_peering_connection_options" "peer-prop" {
  vpc_peering_connection_id = aws_vpc_peering.gpu-peer.id
  accepter { allow_remote_vpc_dns_resolution = true }
  requester { allow_remote_vpc_dns_resolution = true }
}
```
maya: plan shows only the new route + peering option change, not touching infra-wide route tables
ben: tagging for security review? we usually want a sec-review label on changes that alter egress for gpu workloads
maya: added `security:needs-review` label to the PR and linked the eval notes for the workload that will use it
infra-ci: CI report — terraform fmt: OK, tflint: OK, plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy. apply blocked: requires 2 infra approvals and a security approval.
achao: happy to approve infra side once aj or ben confirm no dependency on shared natgw config. also can you confirm this won't affect route propagation for the analytics subnet?
maya: confirmed — analytics uses a different route table id (var.analytics_route_table_id). I ran `terraform plan -target=module.gpu` locally and diff only showed gpu resources.
lex: I can take a look in ~90m. if you need faster, @aj can we tag you to merge during the next canary window?
aj: I can review now. quick note: prefer splitting the peering options into a separate commit so it's easy to roll back if needed. otherwise LGTM pending sec approval. :+1:
ben: sec approved — checked the egress policy and it's consistent with the GPU workload S3/export rules. :shield:
maya: awesome, thanks all. I'll split the peering change into a separate commit and ping back when CI is green. planning to merge in the 23:00 UTC canary window unless anyone objects. :calendar:
lex: no objections from my side.
maya: update — pushed new commit and retriggered CI. infra-ci: plan OK, apply still blocked for approvals.
maya: pinging for final infra approval @aj @lex : can we get the second infra approval so this can go through tonight? :pray:
aj: approving now.
lex: approve. good to go after canary window. :rocket:
